source.title: Greedy Alignment Principle for Optimizer Hyperparameter Selection

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports train loss and held-out performance for SGD+Momentum, Adam, and AdamW under fixed and dynamically selected momentum settings. This bears conceptually on V4's optimizer and tuning effects, but does not test the broader optimizer comparisons across benchmarks described there.
record.gate_note: The paper measures optimizer and momentum effects on training loss and held-out accuracy, relevant to V4. It does not test V1–V3 or V5–V8. Its alignment scores are part of its optimizer-selection method, not measurements of properties that track the training–test gap.
record.test_reason: The separately reported SGD+Momentum and Adam experiments provide an optimizer-family comparison for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 relevant to V4. Momentum is swept, but learning rates, schedules and weight decay are prescribed rather than jointly tuned. Comparisons of K-Switch with fixed momentum within one optimizer family do not independently test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present K-Switch as online greedy momentum selection that generally matches or improves the best reported fixed-momentum baselines and reduces sweep costs. Their objective concerns local training-loss decrease, with no global convergence, validation-loss or population-optimality guarantee. The results include near parity and individual task regressions, so the paper's occasional claim of consistent outperformance is too strong.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes online K-Switch selection by normalized gradient-update alignment, rather than testing the original studies' optimizer comparisons or generalization interventions. It reports train loss and validation/test performance for selected momentum settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with optimizer momentum and candidate range, dataset/task, and fine-tuning setup; the paper reports changing candidate preferences over training and abrupt changes around learning-rate decay.

fits_no_version.finding: K-Switch SGD improves CIFAR-100 accuracy from 77.57% to 78.06% with two candidates and 78.33% with five.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Online momentum selection can improve held-out performance over the best tested fixed momentum within SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: K-Switch Adam reduces training loss from 0.0324 to 0.0115 while accuracy changes from 73.20% to 73.26%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Improved optimization within Adam need not produce a comparable held-out accuracy improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: Within AdamW, dynamic momentum yields small average gains on math and ViT tasks and larger gains on Commonsense-170K full fine-tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The held-out benefit of online AdamW momentum selection varies across tasks and fine-tuning regimes.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: The empirical comparisons focus on a small set of models and tasks. Some reported improvements are small and tables give mean ± std. rather than significance tests. The authors state the greedy objective does not guarantee global convergence, validation loss, or population optimality.
record.rows_left_out: Individual task-level scores from Tables 5 and 6 and the remaining fixed-β1 scores in Table 15 and Table 16 are not separately extracted; the tables report many separately varying task and momentum conditions, and the included rows retain the aggregate comparisons and the principal ResNet-18 momentum sweep within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the contrast between natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width changes beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule tuning protocol; adaptive inferiority despite equal or better training performance; broader tuning removing or reversing an optimizer-family deficit; controlled decoupled-weight-decay and Adam-to-SGD switching comparisons; language-model optimizer-family rankings and word-level language modeling.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Controlled dropout or dropout-plus-weight-decay removal comparisons.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. V4 evidence comes from comparing its separately reported optimizer-family baselines; the primary K-Switch evaluations concern within-family tuning. Extreme-momentum SGD failures qualify the observed ranking rather than challenge V4's statement that adaptive methods often perform worse. All assessments use only the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

Comparisons across the broader image-classification and language benchmarks and optimizer families in the version; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language-model results.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
